newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S. Korea officials detail financial reform draft.
newsitem.headline: S. Korea officials detail financial reform draft.

text.p: South Korea's Presidential Commission for Financial Reform has produced a final draft of its proposals for short-term changes to the banking and financial system, officials said on Wednesday.
The commission, composed of bankers, business leaders and scholars, will soon start work on separate proposals for medium-and long-term reform.
The following are the highlights of its initial recommendations based on interviews with commission members. An official version is expected to be released next week.

- Improve monetary control by: adopting a mix of money-supply indices; establishing an early warning system to monitor inflows and outflows of hot money; adopting central bank swaps and a foreign exchange trading tax.

- Help small and medium-sized firms by: providing them with government funds instead of bank "policy loans"; issuing long-term state bonds to raise funds to help such companies; encouraging pension funds to buy bonds issued by financial institutions to help small firms.

- Boost savings by: extending the maturity of savings instruments aimed at workers; cutting the maturity of long-term savings products linked to home purchases; promoting complex financial instruments; introducing a corporate pension system.
- Improve credit information by allowing financial institutions to share information on borrowers and establishing private credit rating companies.
- Reduce bad debts of financial institutions by strengthening disclosure rules.
- Allow financial institutions greater management say in regulatory and other bodies in which they have invested.
- Replace the "basket" system of controlling total borrowings by big conglomerates, or chaebol, with system monitoring loans to chaebol by individual institutions.
- Immediately allow domestic non-financial companies to enter overseas non-banking financial sector.

- Help small and medium-sized firms by: offering tax breaks to venture capital firms; raising the ceiling on foreign currency-denominated loans to smaller firms; allowing foreign investment in guaranteed bonds issued by smaller firms.
- Lift remaining controls on interest rates.
- Advance timetable for freeing stock brokerage fees.

- Speed up deregulation by: setting up a body to review regulatory practices; banning government intervention in bank personnel management; scrapping controls on real estate investment by top-10 chaebol.
- Ease rules on new branches by financial institutions.

- Strengthen financial institutions by: allowing the top-five chaebol to appoint non-permanent board members in banks; banning individuals who have been punished by supervisory bodies from becoming bank executives.
- Allow non-bank financial institutions greater access to inter-bank on-line computer networks.

- Deregulate financial industry by; lowering barriers between banks, securities houses and insurers; allowing banks to issue bonds; allowing stock brokerages to do foreign exchange and commercial paper-related business; allowing merchant banks to broker securities and lead-manage initial public offerings; allowing merchant banks and investment trust firms to become stock brokerages.
- Improve lending by: establishing unified regulations governing credit card, instalment financing, industrial leasing and venture capital business.
